text:
ops-bot: [ALERT] prod-usw2 inference 5xx rate + latency spike. Auto-scaler reporting GPU node drains. Metric: gpu.xid_errors count rising across multiple racks. https://monitoring.internal/alert/8472 :rotating_light:
Maya: seeing that too. Requests are timing out and LBs are marking backends unhealthy. Capacity down ~12% in us-west-2 GPU pool. Can oncall triage? @SRE Oncall
SRE Oncall: on it. Can someone paste top 10 hosts by Xid count and last boot time?
MonitoringBot: top_hits (last 15m):
```
host-gpu-12-usw2 - Xid: 47 (21), ECC corrected: 129
host-gpu-23-usw2 - Xid: 31 (17), ECC corrected: 98
host-gpu-07-usw2 - Xid: 31 (13), ECC corrected: 76
host-gpu-41-usw2 - Xid: 63 (9), ECC corrected: 54
host-gpu-18-usw2 - Xid: 47 (8), ECC corrected: 43
```
Liam: looks like a fleet-wide pattern, not single rack. Running `dmesg | grep -i Xid` shows repeated `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:xx:00): 31` on several hosts. Also check `nvidia-smi -q | grep -i ecc`
Diego: draining the 6 worst hosts now (`kubectl drain host-gpu-12-usw2 ...`). Marked them unschedulable and starting replacement workflow.
Tara: affected routes are heavy on `redwood-base-3b-quant` in us-west-2. Product reports 8% request failures for chat endpoints. Can we failover traffic to eu-west1 / us-east1 pools temporarily?
Maya: yes please. Start shifting canaries and increase fallback capacity. Note: fallback to CPU-backed variants will increase cost but keep SLAs.
SRE Oncall: Infra, any recent changes? Driver/kernel updates pushed in the last 24h?
Infra-Bot: 1772400000 - kernel-5.15.102 and nvidia-driver-525 deployed to 60% of us-west-2 GPU hosts yesterday (rollout_job_992). Ticket: https://infra.internal/rollouts/992
Liam: hmm that matches timeline. Some vendors flagged driver 525 series with higher corrected ECC rates on certain HBM batches. Worth opening vendor escalation and pausing the driver rollout.
Diego: confirmed logs include both `ECC corrected` and `Xid 31` followed by GPU resets on affected hosts. Opening vendor ticket now and attaching dmesg + `nvidia-smi -q` dumps. ETA for hardware vendor initial reply ~2h.
Maya: temporary mitigations: 1) pause driver rollout and rollback where feasible, 2) exclude affected hosts from scheduling, 3) route traffic to alternate regions/pools, 4) reduce batch sizes for low-latency routes (less stress on memory paths). Will apply 2 & 3 immediately.
Liam: also recommend disabling prefix/KV caching on models hitting these hosts until replacements complete. That reduces memory pressure and KV churn.
Diego: replacement/repair plan: reprovision 20 nodes (hot-swap) across racks A-D. Node replacement in progress, ~45m until first 8 nodes back online, full capacity ~2.5h.
SRE Oncall: action items: Diego -> continue replacements and vendor ticket; Liam -> prepare rollback playbook for driver; Maya -> coordinate traffic shifts and product comms; Tara -> track customer-facing impact and opt-in alerts. We'll post a summary to #incidents once we have vendor response. :thumbsup:
Maya: logging this as a SEV-ish incident and will capture timeline. Please paste any additional logs to this thread.
Infra-Bot: vendor ticket created: HV-12345. Attachments: dmesg.gz, nvidia-smi.json, node-list.csv
Tara: noted. I'll trigger extra support for paying customers in the affected regions.
SRE Oncall: recording for postmortem. If anyone sees new hosts flip, ping here immediately.
Maya: thanks team — keep updates short and frequent.
